title: Kaishika Offers His Kingdom
story:
Krishna came to Vidarbha as a guest, and by every ordinary measure he came with nothing. He had slain Kamsa, yet he had not taken the throne of Mathura for himself. He had no city, no crown, no seat among the kings gathered at Kundina for the swayamvara of the princess. The proud among them had already settled the matter in their own minds, echoing the taunt of the emperor Jarasandha: Devaki's son has never been installed, he holds no city — how shall he sit in the same assembly as kings?

But there were two who saw it differently. Kratha and Kaishika, the brothers who ruled Vidarbha, watched the visitor and thought not of his lack but of their own. In his mind Kaishika turned it over quietly: if we can but behold the consecration of this man, our sins will be washed away; his presence will purify our understanding. What hospitality can we possibly offer one for whom there is no worthier person in the three worlds? What gift could be enough? And in the turning of that question they found the answer, for the only thing worthy of such a guest was the whole of what they ruled.

The answer they settled on was everything. The two brothers went to Krishna and bowed their heads low before him. Blessed is our birth and our fame today, they said; blessed are our ancestors, since you have come to our house. Then they laid it all at his feet — their umbrellas and flagstaffs, their throne, their army, their flourishing city. You were once anointed by Indra himself as Upendra, they reminded him; we now install you in our kingdom. What we two do, no numberless host of kings, not even Jarasandha himself, will be able to undo.

There was a reason for the urgency. The king Bhishmaka, father of the maiden, had seen the trouble brewing among the assembled kings and, after consulting the brothers, had prepared a fine resting house for Krishna, so that no dispute over seats might break the gathering apart. Perform the royal unction today, the brothers urged, and tomorrow be seated at ease on an auspicious throne, installed before all the kings as emperor at the behest of Indra.

So they sent an emissary among the kings. And there, in the assembly, Kaishika rose to speak of what had just occurred. His eldest brother Kratha had conferred the kingdom upon Krishna. But the moment Kratha had said, Sit on this seat, an invisible voice had spoken from the sky.

The voice was Indra's own envoy, and his words were plain. Do not offer him the seat on which you have sat, the celestial voice said. The king of gods has sent, for him alone, a white seat of gold, built by the celestial architect, crested with gems and marked with the emblem of a lion. Place him upon it with the other kings, and sprinkle him. And whoever among the kings assembled here for the maiden fails to come, shall be slain by the king of gods. Eight jars of celestial gold and jewels, born of the treasures of the lord of riches, will come among you to install this emperor.

Kaishika told the kings what followed. The emissary delivered the seat, bright as the rising sun, and then returned to the city of the gods. Now, he said, let every king here behold the one whom the king of gods has himself recognized — dreadful, irresistible, wonderful in form, a sight rare in the land of mortals. If we witness this ceremony, the bathing of the God of gods, surely our sins will be destroyed.

The offer had been made, and the heavens had already answered it.
reflection: The brothers' gesture matters because of what it reverses. Jarasandha measures a man by his city and his crown, and finds Krishna lacking; Kratha and Kaishika, looking at the same man, can think only of what they might give him. Their kingdom is not a sacrifice but a recognition — and the answer from the sky confirms that they have seen truly.
next_story_tease: But the white seat was only the beginning; a consecration unlike any on earth was about to fall from the sky itself.
hero_scene: Kratha and Kaishika, the two kings of Vidarbha, bowing low before Krishna as they offer him their umbrellas, throne, army and city, while above them an unseen voice announces the white seat of gold sent by Indra.
visual_elements: Krishna arriving as a guest with Garuda
the white seat of gold marked with a lion emblem
the celestial emissary's voice from the sky
the resting house prepared by Bhishmaka
